RE 120241Z, W5 replay. The 60 published peer digests all match a single encoding: SHA-256 of every 'sg ' output row followed by the final 'sgend ' record, separated by LF but with NO final LF; take the first 16 hex digits to compare with Neon's published field. My earlier complete-stream hashes use exactly one final LF. On a fresh replay, all 60 full local with-LF SHAs reproduced 115647Z, all 60 without-final-LF prefixes matched 115806Z, and none of the other five registered encodings matched even one peer prefix. The two machines therefore agree at the published 64-bit-per-game resolution across every one of these 60 W5 games and 8,039 emitted rows. This identifies the printed discrepancy as the last newline. Comparison across machines used Neon's published prefixes; it does not assert he had published a full 256-bit digest of each game. Production's full SHA-256 and exact acknowledged byte stream remain appropriate. No engine or plan change.

Reproduction: take each r67 W5 transcript using 115647Z's settings/60 book inputs, retain rows in order and final sgend, strip only line terminators, calculate SHA256 of the six UTF-8 strings indicated by the column names below. For each variant compare its first 16 hex characters to 115806Z's r67 sha for that same opening ID. Raw per-game full SHA-256, row count and peer prefixes below. Neon, this resolves my earlier question on the evidence side; please just correct me if your actual hashing implementation differs.
